scenes.headline: How Husky gets more tokens from each read
scenes.sub: A bus-bound decoder, prompt lookup and a trained draft.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Axolotl! Husky claims up to four and a half times Apple's MLX on a Mac. Here's how.

scenes.text: At batch one, every token streams all 2.4 GB of weights through the memory bus. No engine reads faster, so Husky gets more tokens per read.
scenes.say: At batch one, every token streams all two point four gigabytes of weights through the memory bus. So Husky gets more tokens per read.

scenes.title: The ceiling for one token per read
scenes.say: First, the ceiling for one token per read.

parts.note: MLX's median: 159 tokens a second, 6.29 ms each
parts.say: MLX's median is six point two nine milliseconds a token.

parts.note: Husky's own floor for one plain streaming read
parts.say: Husky puts the floor for a plain read at four point five.
So kernels win at most one point four times. Without a draft, Husky sits under that line, at one point one two five.

scenes.title: Two ways to guess, one way to check

steps.say: Guess one, prompt lookup: if the last few tokens appear in the prompt, propose the seven that followed. No model needed.
Guess two: the Flash draft, a single small layer reading Woof's own hidden states. It proposes seven too.
Woof checks every guess in one eight-row step, for about one and a half times a single row's cost.

steps.note: On edits, typically five or six survive each read
steps.say: It keeps the tokens it agrees with, so the output never changes. On edits, typically five or six survive.

scenes.title: Gain over MLX across sixteen tasks
scenes.note: Medians, except the headline, which is the single best row
scenes.say: Across sixteen tasks: one point one two five without a draft, one point seven six with Flash. The four point four eight is one edit row.

scenes.title: Flash on, replayed
scenes.credit: Underdog's own launch animation; its measurements

steps.say: Underdog's own launch animation replays one typo-fixing edit, from measured timings. It is not a screen recording.
With Flash on, Husky is done at five hundred and thirty-seven tokens a second. MLX is still writing.

scenes.text: At batch one, kernels can't outrun the bus. Speed comes from tokens per read, so compare speculation with speculation.

scenes.say: The bus caps every read, and speculation fills each read with more tokens.
